sourceLessons.title: Use your voice instead of typing
sourceLessons.prerequisites: A microphone. Enable voice features in Settings → Voice & Vision.

steps.title: Turn on voice features
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Voice & Vision and enable Enable voice features. Start with Whisper (local, free) for Speech-to-text and Piper (local neural, free) for Text-to-speech. Click Save changes. Listening and speaking are separate choices; they do not change your main AI model.
steps.checkpoint: Voice is enabled and the choices are saved.

steps.title: Dictate into the message box
steps.narrationDraft: Click the microphone beside the message box and speak clearly. Dictation turns speech into draft text. Stop recording using the microphone control, check the recognised words, edit any mistake, then press Send. This gives you a chance to correct names, numbers and dates before sending.
steps.checkpoint: Your spoken words appear as editable text in the draft.
steps.tip: The first use may take a moment while the local speech engine loads. Check the selected microphone and Windows permission if it cannot start.

steps.title: Choose conversation for an ongoing exchange
steps.narrationDraft: The Voice entry opens an ongoing spoken exchange rather than simply filling the draft. The circle beside it opens the minimal orb view. In conversation mode, spoken turns are sent as the conversation proceeds. Use the mute and exit controls when you want it to stop listening.
steps.checkpoint: You can distinguish draft dictation from an ongoing voice session.

steps.title: Listen to an existing reply
steps.narrationDraft: Use a reply’s read-aloud control when you want to hear text already on screen. Autonomous speech in Voice settings controls when Genesis may speak without a play click. Choose On request only if you want quiet unless you explicitly ask for speech.
steps.checkpoint: You have chosen when Genesis may speak.

sourceLessons.title: Improve speech recognition
sourceLessons.prerequisites: Settings → Voice & Vision. Internet for an optional download.

steps.title: Speech-to-text listens; it does not answer
steps.narrationDraft: Whisper turns audio into words. Your language model then answers those words. Changing Whisper changes recognition, not the brain’s knowledge or personality. The bundled base model gets you started. A larger recognition model can help with other languages and harder audio, at a memory and speed cost.
steps.checkpoint: You know which part is recognising your voice.

steps.title: Choose the languages you speak
steps.narrationDraft: Use Languages you speak → Add a language. Selecting your languages helps avoid a similar language being mistaken for yours. Leave the list empty only if you want recognition to consider any language. A single Whisper model supports multiple languages; you do not need a separate download for each language.
steps.checkpoint: The languages you actually use appear in the list.

steps.title: Pick a size and download it
steps.narrationDraft: Open Whisper model. Automatic chooses the recommended size for this computer once available. A missing size offers a Download button and shows its size. Click Download and wait for completion. Progress can resume after a dropped connection. Choose the size, then save changes.
steps.checkpoint: The selected model is installed, and you have checked “In use now.”

steps.title: Read In use now
steps.narrationDraft: The size you choose and the size currently running can differ. If a size is not downloaded or does not fit in free memory, Genesis uses an installed size that fits. In use now tells you which one is actually active. Freeing memory or choosing a smaller size can help on an older computer.
steps.checkpoint: You can explain why “Automatic small” might currently be using base.

steps.title: Leave the device on Automatic to start
steps.narrationDraft: Whisper device → Automatic uses the NVIDIA graphics card only when there is room and a local AI model is not competing for it. Otherwise recognition uses the processor. Selecting graphics-card recognition may require the optional NVIDIA libraries, offered with a download button. The processor remains a useful choice.
steps.checkpoint: The “Running on” line tells you the active device.

steps.title: Try a short sentence and compare
steps.narrationDraft: Dictate a short sentence with a name and a number. Correct any mistakes in the draft. If recognition is poor, reduce background noise, check your languages, and compare an installed larger size. Voice resources → Auto · save memory unloads idle engines; an active session is protected.
steps.checkpoint: Your next dictated sentence is understandable without a long wait.

sourceLessons.title: Choose and download a speaking voice
sourceLessons.prerequisites: Voice enabled. Internet only for a new voice download.

steps.title: Text-to-speech is the speaking part
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Voice & Vision → Text-to-speech. Piper is a local neural voice. Windows voices use installed system voices. Browser voices depend on the browser environment. The voice choice belongs to its selected engine; changing the engine changes the available voices.
steps.checkpoint: You have chosen the engine that will speak.

steps.title: Choose an installed voice
steps.narrationDraft: Open Voice and select an installed voice. The bundled Piper voice is Amy in US English. Choose a voice appropriate for the language you want spoken. Custom… lets you enter a known voice name or ID; it does not create or download a new voice by itself.
steps.checkpoint: Your selected voice appears in the field.

steps.title: Download another Piper voice
steps.narrationDraft: With Piper selected, use Download a voice…, choose a catalog entry, then click Download. Wait for Downloaded or Already installed. The successful download selects that voice. Click Save changes, then use read-aloud on a short reply to hear it.
steps.checkpoint: The new voice is available and speaks a short test.

steps.title: Choose when it speaks
steps.narrationDraft: Set Autonomous speech to On request only, Urgent / important, or Everything (natural pacing). These choices control spontaneous speech. They do not mean the microphone is always listening. An ongoing voice conversation has its own mute and exit controls.
steps.checkpoint: Genesis speaks only as often as you intended.

steps.title: Effects and the HAL choices
steps.narrationDraft: Voice effect → HAL 9000 changes the pitch, pace and room reverb of a local Piper or Windows voice. Set up HAL 9000 voice for me sets an effect and downloads the chosen local voice; save afterward. The separate HAL 9000 — real voice (clone, sidecar) engine needs its own running sidecar service. An effect is different from that separate engine.
steps.checkpoint: You know whether you selected an effect or a separate voice engine.

steps.title: If the chosen voice cannot speak
steps.narrationDraft: A missing configured Piper voice can use bundled Amy. Local speech can fall back to Windows and then browser speech when available. Check the voice status and test again. Genesis does not silently switch a local voice to a paid cloud service. An unavailable cloud or sidecar engine should be checked in its own configuration.
steps.checkpoint: You know how to get speech working again without enabling a cloud provider.

sourceLessons.title: Use cloud listening or cloud voices
sourceLessons.prerequisites: Internet and the matching provider’s API key or voice credentials.

steps.title: Listening and speaking can be mixed
steps.narrationDraft: You can listen locally and speak with a cloud voice, or use cloud listening and local speech. They are independent. Your main model can still be local. Choose each part in Settings → Voice & Vision and save. Cloud recognition sends audio to that provider; cloud speech sends the text to be spoken.
steps.checkpoint: You know which part, if any, will use a cloud service.

steps.title: For cloud recognition, choose OpenAI STT
steps.narrationDraft: Set Speech-to-text → OpenAI STT (cloud) and enter its key in STT API key. This field is separate from the main model’s key. Save and try a short recording. The Whisper size and device controls describe the local recognition route; they do not tune the cloud service.
steps.checkpoint: A small recording is recognised using the selected provider.

steps.title: For a cloud voice, choose its engine
steps.narrationDraft: Under Text-to-speech, choose OpenAI (cloud), ElevenLabs (cloud) or Azure (cloud). Enter the appropriate TTS API key and choose a voice supported by that engine, or use Custom for a known voice ID. This picture shows the OpenAI choice; select your own provider. Use the provider’s required configuration; an Azure credential or provider-specific voice identifier may need additional setup.
steps.checkpoint: The engine, credential and voice belong to the same provider.

steps.title: Save and test before a long conversation
steps.narrationDraft: Click Save changes. Play one short reply. Check connectivity, key access and the voice identifier if it fails. Provider charges and quotas are controlled by that company. Local voice never changes to cloud automatically: you explicitly choose the cloud engine and supply its key.
steps.checkpoint: You hear a short test in the voice you selected.

sourceLessons.title: Have a conversation with the orb
sourceLessons.prerequisites: The Modern interface, a connected model and working voice input/output.

steps.title: Open the circle beside Voice
steps.narrationDraft: In Modern, find Voice near the bottom of the left panel. Click its small circle for the orb conversation. Genesis opens a minimal screen and starts the voice session when ready. This is an ongoing conversation: your spoken turns go to the model without pressing Send for each one.
steps.checkpoint: The orb view opens and reports its voice state.

steps.title: Follow the words beneath the orb
steps.narrationDraft: The state tells you what is happening: Opening microphone, Listening, Waiting for your next words, Transcribing, Thinking, or Speaking. A brief pause can let it gather your next words before sending the turn. If it is thinking, give it a moment to work.
steps.checkpoint: You can tell whether it is listening or answering.

steps.title: Move the pointer to reveal controls
steps.narrationDraft: Move your mouse over the orb view to show controls. The microphone button mutes listening; the speaker button mutes sound. They are separate. Use the left chevrons to show the transcript and the right chevrons to show the browser panel. Panels can be resized.
steps.checkpoint: You can mute listening without losing the conversation.

steps.title: Interrupt when you want to speak
steps.narrationDraft: While it is thinking or speaking, tap the orb to interrupt the reply and speak. The microphone’s mute state still matters. Interrupting a voice reply is not the same as undoing an action or stopping every background task. Use the work controls for that.
steps.checkpoint: You know how to interrupt the spoken turn.

steps.title: Read along or watch browsing
steps.narrationDraft: Open Transcript to see the words and tool activity. Open Browser when Genesis uses its browser. Closing the browser panel hides the view; it does not mean all browser work has stopped. If a site needs you, follow the request and return control when ready.
steps.checkpoint: You can reveal the transcript while keeping the orb visible.

steps.title: End the session deliberately
steps.narrationDraft: Click the exit icon or press Escape to leave the focused orb conversation. End or mute the session when you do not want it listening. If audio recovery offers Retry audio, Save audio or Discard & reset, read that notice before choosing.
steps.checkpoint: You are back in the main interface and the voice session has ended.

sourceLessons.title: Give a text-only model the ability to see
sourceLessons.prerequisites: A working saved preset for a model that actually accepts images.

steps.title: The helper sees; your main model still answers
steps.narrationDraft: A language model that only reads text cannot see pixels. Genesis can ask a separate vision model to describe an image, then give that description to your main model. Think of one helper looking at a photograph and explaining it to another helper. This does not change the main model’s underlying abilities.
steps.checkpoint: You understand the two-model arrangement.

steps.title: Save the image model as a preset
steps.narrationDraft: First add and test the picture-capable model in Settings → Models. It may be local or cloud. Set Image input to Auto-detect, unless provider metadata is missing or wrong and you know the correct capability. Choosing “Vision / multimodal” does not make a text-only model capable of seeing.
steps.checkpoint: The secondary preset points to a real image-capable model.

steps.title: Choose the Secondary vision model
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Voice & Vision → Screen & desktop control. Under Secondary vision model, select that saved preset. It has its own provider, connection and model. A cloud helper can receive pictures even when your main language model runs locally; choose a local helper if you want that image processing local.
steps.checkpoint: The intended image model is selected.

steps.title: Choose how images are routed
steps.narrationDraft: Auto: primary → secondary fallback uses the resolved model if it can accept images, and the secondary when needed. Always use secondary preset sends every image through the selected helper. Disabled turns image-model routing off. The Legacy options exist for older dedicated configurations; a saved secondary preset is easier to manage.
steps.checkpoint: The selected routing choice matches what you want.

steps.title: Read the effective route, then try a picture
steps.narrationDraft: Click Save changes and check Effective route. A model may say it will be tested on first use until image input has been verified. Attach a simple picture and ask “Describe what you see.” Confirm the description is right before asking it to reason about a tiny label or complicated screen.
steps.checkpoint: The image is described correctly and the route status makes sense.

steps.title: Understand the limit of the handoff
steps.narrationDraft: Your text-only model reasons from the helper’s description, not from the original pixels. If the helper misses a detail, the main answer can miss it too. Ask for a specific region or a clearer screenshot. A local language model plus local vision helper keeps those model calls local; web tools and other cloud choices remain separate.
steps.checkpoint: You know why checking the image description matters.

steps.title: Screen reading has extra tools
steps.narrationDraft: OCR engine reads written text from a screen. Maximum Set-of-Marks targets limits numbered controls in a vision pass. These help screen tasks but do not replace permission to control an app. Computer use decides what Genesis may operate. The vision route is also used by image-file tools and Missions.
steps.checkpoint: You can distinguish reading the screen from permission to act on it.

sourceLessons.title: Show Genesis the window you are using
sourceLessons.prerequisites: Genesis desktop on Windows and another app window you want to show.

steps.title: Enable the screenshot shortcut
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Computer use → Appshots and turn on Enable Appshots. This desktop preference applies immediately. The status should say the shortcut is ready. You can also choose whether a sound plays after capture.
steps.checkpoint: The shortcut reports ready.

steps.title: Bring the other app to the front
steps.narrationDraft: Open the window you want to show Genesis. Press Left Alt + Right Alt together. Release both keys before taking another screenshot. Appshots captures the foreground app’s visible window and puts the image into your current conversation draft.
steps.checkpoint: The screenshot appears attached to the draft.

steps.title: Explain what you want and send
steps.narrationDraft: Return to Genesis. Check the screenshot, write something like “Explain this error message” or “Which button opens the settings?”, then press Send. The shortcut does not send the screenshot by itself. Your selected image route reads it after you send.
steps.checkpoint: The image and your question are sent together.

steps.title: Check before sharing
steps.narrationDraft: If the picture shows a private letter, key or personal information you did not intend to share, remove it from the draft. Choose a local vision route when you want picture interpretation to stay local. The screenshot only shows what was visible at capture time; it is not a live screen stream.
steps.checkpoint: You are sending exactly the window content you intended.

audio.rationale: Video-4 source decodes to 239.8535s. Its first 7s are a quieter opening before the strong section; preserve that opening once. Repeat from 7.5s, end at 232.5s before the late 233–236s dynamic break and 239s near-silence. The repeat span is 225s with 9s equal-power qsin overlaps, giving 216s spacing. Four-second entrance and eight-second final fade. Derived from this track’s measured envelope; inspect every rendered join, entire-bed silence and loudness. No continuous subjective-listening claim.

one change
items: Say: “Mira needs 12 pots on Friday.”
Read the names and numbers in the draft
Reduce noise and check the selected languages
Compare one installed recognition size at a time
scenes.note: Auto · save memory unloads idle engines. First use can load them again; an active voice session is protected.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: Your next dictated sentence is understandable without a long wait.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Lesson
complete
items: Check the actual status and a small test
Keep listening, answering and speaking separate
Review what is sent and which route receives it
Return to any step with the lesson chapter
scenes.note: Continue at your own pace. A saved setting and a real successful test provide different evidence.

scenes.title:
A voice
you choose.
scenes.body:
Choose and download a speaking voice
Installed voices, downloads, effects and recovery.

scenes.title:
Before
you begin
items: Voice enabled. Internet only for a new voice download.
scenes.note: Prepare these prerequisites before you try the lesson. Pause whenever you need time in Genesis.

scenes.title:
Choose the
speaking engine
scenes.body: Open Settings → Voice & Vision → Text-to-speech. Piper is a local neural voice. Windows voices use installed system voices. Browser voices depend on the browser environment.
scenes.callout: Text-to-speech
scenes.note: Step 1 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Choose the
speaking engine
scenes.body: The voice choice belongs to its selected engine; changing the engine changes the available voices.
scenes.callout: Text-to-speech
scenes.note: Step 1 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Match engine
and voice
items: Piper: locally installed neural voice files
Windows: installed system voices
Browser: available browser voices
Each engine has its own voice choices
scenes.note: A voice ID from another engine may not work. Pick the engine first, then its supported voice.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You have chosen the engine that will speak.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Choose an
installed voice
scenes.body: Open Voice and select an installed voice. The bundled Piper voice is Amy in US English. Choose a voice appropriate for the language you want spoken.
scenes.callout: Voice: installed Amy · English (US)
scenes.note: Step 2 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Choose an
installed voice
scenes.body: Custom… lets you enter a known voice name or ID; it does not create or download a new voice by itself.
scenes.callout: Voice: installed Amy · English (US)
scenes.note: Step 2 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Start with
bundled Amy
items: Choose Piper as the speaking engine
Choose Amy · English (US)
Save changes and play one short reply
Custom accepts an existing name or ID
scenes.note: Custom does not synthesise a new voice identity or download missing files. Choose a voice for the spoken language.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: Your selected voice appears in the field.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Download a
Piper voice
scenes.body: With Piper selected, use Download a voice…, choose a catalog entry, then click Download. Wait for Downloaded or Already installed. The successful download selects that voice.
scenes.callout: Select a catalog voice, then Download
scenes.note: Step 3 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Download a
Piper voice
scenes.body: Click Save changes, then use read-aloud on a short reply to hear it.
scenes.callout: Select a catalog voice, then Download
scenes.note: Step 3 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A catalog
download example
items: Choose a wanted entry in Download a voice…
Press Download and wait for success
The downloaded voice becomes selected
Save changes and play a short reply
scenes.note: Ryan is one example catalog entry. Use a voice available in your current catalog; this fixture performs no download.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The new voice is available and speaks a short test.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Choose when
it speaks
scenes.body: Set Autonomous speech to On request only, Urgent / important, or Everything (natural pacing). These choices control spontaneous speech.
scenes.callout: Autonomous speech
scenes.note: Step 4 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Choose when
it speaks
scenes.body: They do not mean the microphone is always listening. An ongoing voice conversation has its own mute and exit controls.
scenes.callout: Autonomous speech
scenes.note: Step 4 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Choose your
speech rhythm
items: On request only: ask or play explicitly
Urgent / important: selected spontaneous speech
Everything: natural pacing
Mute and exit belong to the ongoing session
scenes.note: Spontaneous speech and microphone listening are different decisions. Check both when you want quiet.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: Genesis speaks only as often as you intended.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Effect or
separate engine?
scenes.body: Voice effect → HAL 9000 changes the pitch, pace and room reverb of a local Piper or Windows voice.
scenes.callout: Voice effect: separate from the HAL sidecar engine
scenes.note: Step 5 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 3. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Effect or
separate engine?
scenes.body: Set up HAL 9000 voice for me sets an effect and downloads the chosen local voice; save afterward.
scenes.callout: Voice effect: separate from the HAL sidecar engine
scenes.note: Step 5 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Effect or
separate engine?
scenes.body: The separate HAL 9000 — real voice (clone, sidecar) engine needs its own running sidecar service. An effect is different from that separate engine.
scenes.callout: Voice effect: separate from the HAL sidecar engine
scenes.note: Step 5 of 6 · Teaching 3 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Two HAL
choices
items: HAL 9000 effect processes a local voice
The setup action selects an effect and voice
Save after the local voice setup completes
Real voice (clone, sidecar) needs its own service
scenes.note: A pitch, pace and reverb effect is different from the separate HAL voice engine. Choose the one you intend.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You know whether you selected an effect or a separate voice engine.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Get local
speech back
scenes.body: A missing configured Piper voice can use bundled Amy. Local speech can fall back to Windows and then browser speech when available. Check the voice status and test again.
scenes.callout: Text-to-speech
scenes.note: Step 6 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Get local
speech back
scenes.body: Genesis does not silently switch a local voice to a paid cloud service. An unavailable cloud or sidecar engine should be checked in its own configuration.
scenes.callout: Text-to-speech
scenes.note: Step 6 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Recover
local speech
items: Check the selected Piper voice is installed
Bundled Amy can replace a missing Piper voice
Local fallback can use Windows, then browser
Check status, mute and one short read-aloud test
scenes.note: An unavailable cloud or sidecar engine needs its own configuration checked. Local fallback does not silently enable paid cloud.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You know how to get speech working again without enabling a cloud provider.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Lesson
complete
items: Check the actual status and a small test
Keep listening, answering and speaking separate
Review what is sent and which route receives it
Return to any step with the lesson chapter
scenes.note: Continue at your own pace. A saved setting and a real successful test provide different evidence.

scenes.title:
Local or cloud.
Your choice.
scenes.body:
Use cloud listening or cloud voices
Independent audio routes and matching credentials.

scenes.title:
Before
you begin
items: Internet and the matching provider’s API key or voice credentials.
scenes.note: Prepare these prerequisites before you try the lesson. Pause whenever you need time in Genesis.

scenes.title:
Mix listening
and speaking
scenes.body: You can listen locally and speak with a cloud voice, or use cloud listening and local speech. They are independent. Your main model can still be local.
scenes.callout: Speech-to-text: choose the listening engine
scenes.note: Step 1 of 4 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Mix listening
and speaking
scenes.body: Choose each part in Settings → Voice & Vision and save. Cloud recognition sends audio to that provider; cloud speech sends the text to be spoken.
scenes.callout: Speech-to-text: choose the listening engine
scenes.note: Step 1 of 4 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Choose where
each part goes
items: Local recognition + cloud speech is possible
Cloud recognition + local speech is possible
Your main language model can remain local
Cloud listening receives audio; speech receives text
scenes.note: Keep track of each selected route. A local main model does not make an explicitly chosen cloud voice local.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You know which part, if any, will use a cloud service.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Choose cloud
recognition
scenes.body: Set Speech-to-text → OpenAI STT (cloud) and enter its key in STT API key. This field is separate from the main model’s key. Save and try a short recording.
scenes.callout: STT API key: separate listening credential
scenes.note: Step 2 of 4 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Choose cloud
recognition
scenes.body: The Whisper size and device controls describe the local recognition route; they do not tune the cloud service.
scenes.callout: STT API key: separate listening credential
scenes.note: Step 2 of 4 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A separate
listening key
items: Choose OpenAI STT (cloud)
Enter the matching key in STT API key
Save changes, then try one short recording
Check recognised text before a long exchange
scenes.note: Use your own credential only in Genesis. This tutorial contains no real key; local Whisper controls do not tune cloud STT.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: A small recording is recognised using the selected provider.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Match the
cloud voice
scenes.body: Under Text-to-speech, choose OpenAI (cloud), ElevenLabs (cloud) or Azure (cloud).
scenes.callout: Matching TTS engine, voice and key
scenes.note: Step 3 of 4 · Teaching 1 of 4. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Match the
cloud voice
scenes.body: Enter the appropriate TTS API key and choose a voice supported by that engine, or use Custom for a known voice ID.
scenes.callout: Matching TTS engine, voice and key
scenes.note: Step 3 of 4 · Teaching 2 of 4. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Match the
cloud voice
scenes.body: This picture shows the OpenAI choice; select your own provider.
scenes.callout: Matching TTS engine, voice and key
scenes.note: Step 3 of 4 · Teaching 3 of 4. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Match the
cloud voice
scenes.body: Use the provider’s required configuration; an Azure credential or provider-specific voice identifier may need additional setup.
scenes.callout: Matching TTS engine, voice and key
scenes.note: Step 3 of 4 · Teaching 4 of 4. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Keep the
voice details together
items: Choose OpenAI, ElevenLabs or Azure
Use that provider’s TTS credential
Choose its supported voice or known voice ID
Check any provider-specific setup requirements
scenes.note: Azure may require region and voice details beyond an example key. The screenshot illustrates OpenAI only.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The engine, credential and voice belong to the same provider.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Save, then
test briefly
scenes.body: Click Save changes. Play one short reply. Check connectivity, key access and the voice identifier if it fails. Provider charges and quotas are controlled by that company.
scenes.callout: Save changes
scenes.note: Step 4 of 4 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Save, then
test briefly
scenes.body: Local voice never changes to cloud automatically: you explicitly choose the cloud engine and supply its key.
scenes.callout: Save changes
scenes.note: Step 4 of 4 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A ten-word
test first
items: Save the matching engine, credential and voice
Play one short existing reply
Check internet, access and voice ID if silent
Check the provider’s quota and billing
scenes.note: A saved setting does not prove the provider accepted the request. Hear a small test before starting a long conversation.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You hear a short test in the voice you selected.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Lesson
complete
items: Check the actual status and a small test
Keep listening, answering and speaking separate
Review what is sent and which route receives it
Return to any step with the lesson chapter
scenes.note: Continue at your own pace. A saved setting and a real successful test provide different evidence.

scenes.title:
An ongoing
conversation.
scenes.body:
Have a conversation with the orb
States, mute controls, interruptions and ending.

scenes.title:
Before
you begin
items: The Modern interface, a connected model and working voice input/output.
scenes.note: Prepare these prerequisites before you try the lesson. Pause whenever you need time in Genesis.

scenes.title:
Open the
orb conversation
scenes.body: In Modern, find Voice near the bottom of the left panel. Click its small circle for the orb conversation. Genesis opens a minimal screen and starts the voice session when ready.
scenes.callout: Circle beside Voice: ongoing orb conversation
scenes.note: Step 1 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Open the
orb conversation
scenes.body: This is an ongoing conversation: your spoken turns go to the model without pressing Send for each one.
scenes.callout: Circle beside Voice: ongoing orb conversation
scenes.note: Step 1 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Prepare an
ongoing session
items: Use the Modern interface
Check your model connection
Test listening and speaking first
Clear or send your draft before opening the circle
scenes.note: Spoken turns submit as the session proceeds. Dictation’s review-and-Send behavior is a different mode.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The orb view opens and reports its voice state.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Read the
state beneath it
scenes.body: The state tells you what is happening: Opening microphone, Listening, Waiting for your next words, Transcribing, Thinking, or Speaking.
scenes.callout: Read the state text beneath the orb
scenes.note: Step 2 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Read the
state beneath it
scenes.body: A brief pause can let it gather your next words before sending the turn. If it is thinking, give it a moment to work.
scenes.callout: Read the state text beneath the orb
scenes.note: Step 2 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Let the
state guide you
items: Opening microphone: audio is starting
Listening: it can hear your words
Waiting for your next words: gathering a turn
Transcribing, Thinking, Speaking: processing stages
scenes.note: A brief pause can gather more words. Check the state before assuming the conversation has stopped.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You can tell whether it is listening or answering.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Reveal the
controls
scenes.body: Move your mouse over the orb view to show controls. The microphone button mutes listening; the speaker button mutes sound. They are separate.
scenes.callout: Microphone mute and speaker mute are separate
scenes.note: Step 3 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Reveal the
controls
scenes.body: Use the left chevrons to show the transcript and the right chevrons to show the browser panel. Panels can be resized.
scenes.callout: Microphone mute and speaker mute are separate
scenes.note: Step 3 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Two independent
mute controls
items: Move the pointer to reveal controls
Microphone mute stops listening
Speaker mute stops audible output
Reveal transcript and browser with the chevrons
scenes.note: Mute the microphone when you want privacy from listening. Speaker mute alone does not stop microphone input.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You can mute listening without losing the conversation.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Interrupt
a spoken reply
scenes.body: While it is thinking or speaking, tap the orb to interrupt the reply and speak. The microphone’s mute state still matters.
scenes.callout: Tap the orb while thinking or speaking
scenes.note: Step 4 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Interrupt
a spoken reply
scenes.body: Interrupting a voice reply is not the same as undoing an action or stopping every background task. Use the work controls for that.
scenes.callout: Tap the orb while thinking or speaking
scenes.note: Step 4 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
An interruption
example
items: It begins an answer about your garden
Tap the orb while thinking or speaking
If the microphone is muted, unmute to speak
Say: “Use only the sunny windowsill.”
scenes.note: Interrupting the voice reply preserves the microphone’s mute state. Inspect work controls to pause or stop other work.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You know how to interrupt the spoken turn.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Read along
and reveal panels
scenes.body: Open Transcript to see the words and tool activity. Open Browser when Genesis uses its browser.
scenes.callout: Transcript: read the conversation alongside the orb
scenes.note: Step 5 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Read along
and reveal panels
scenes.body: Closing the browser panel hides the view; it does not mean all browser work has stopped. If a site needs you, follow the request and return control when ready.
scenes.callout: Transcript: read the conversation alongside the orb
scenes.note: Step 5 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Keep the
orb visible
scenes.body: The transcript appears beside the orb. Resize its divider to choose how much room the words and the orb receive.
scenes.callout: Left chevrons reveal or hide the transcript
scenes.note: The browser panel has its own right chevrons. Hiding a panel changes the view.

scenes.title:
Read and
watch with context
items: Left chevrons reveal the transcript
Right chevrons reveal the browser panel
Drag a panel divider to resize it
Follow a site’s request when Genesis needs you
scenes.note: Closing the browser panel hides its view. Check work status and controls when you intend to stop browser activity.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You can reveal the transcript while keeping the orb visible.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
End the
session deliberately
scenes.body: Click the exit icon or press Escape to leave the focused orb conversation. End or mute the session when you do not want it listening.
scenes.callout: Exit voice conversation · Escape also exits
scenes.note: Step 6 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
End the
session deliberately
scenes.body: If audio recovery offers Retry audio, Save audio or Discard & reset, read that notice before choosing.
scenes.callout: Exit voice conversation · Escape also exits
scenes.note: Step 6 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Choose an
explicit ending
items: Use the exit icon or press Escape
Check that the session has ended
Retry audio attempts the retained recording
Save audio or Discard & reset are separate choices
scenes.note: Read any recovery notice before acting. Ending or muting is deliberate; leaving the speaker quiet alone is not microphone mute.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You are back in the main interface and the voice session has ended.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Lesson
complete
items: Check the actual status and a small test
Keep listening, answering and speaking separate
Review what is sent and which route receives it
Return to any step with the lesson chapter
scenes.note: Continue at your own pace. A saved setting and a real successful test provide different evidence.

scenes.title:
Give images
a helper.
scenes.body:
Give a text-only model the ability to see
A real image model, routing and the limits of description.

scenes.title:
Before
you begin
items: A working saved preset for a model that actually accepts images.
scenes.note: Prepare these prerequisites before you try the lesson. Pause whenever you need time in Genesis.

scenes.title:
One helper
looks at the image
scenes.body: A language model that only reads text cannot see pixels. Genesis can ask a separate vision model to describe an image, then give that description to your main model.
scenes.callout: Secondary vision model: choose a tested preset
scenes.note: Step 1 of 7 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
One helper
looks at the image
scenes.body: Think of one helper looking at a photograph and explaining it to another helper. This does not change the main model’s underlying abilities.
scenes.callout: Secondary vision model: choose a tested preset
scenes.note: Step 1 of 7 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A photograph
with two helpers
items: Vision helper: looks at the photograph
Helper produces an image description
Text-only main model receives that description
Main model reasons and answers you
scenes.note: If the helper misses a small detail, the main model may miss it too. The main model does not gain image capability.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You understand the two-model arrangement.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Save a real
image model
scenes.body: First add and test the picture-capable model in Settings → Models. It may be local or cloud.
scenes.callout: Image input: declare a real capability
scenes.note: Step 2 of 7 · Teaching 1 of 3. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Save a real
image model
scenes.body: Set Image input to Auto-detect, unless provider metadata is missing or wrong and you know the correct capability.
scenes.callout: Image input: declare a real capability
scenes.note: Step 2 of 7 · Teaching 2 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Save a real
image model
scenes.body: Choosing “Vision / multimodal” does not make a text-only model capable of seeing.
scenes.callout: Image input: declare a real capability
scenes.note: Step 2 of 7 · Teaching 3 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Prove the
image connection
items: Create the image-capable model’s own preset
Use a real installed local or accessible cloud model
Save and test its connection and image input
Keep Auto-detect unless you know metadata is wrong
scenes.note: A capability selector records a declaration. Choosing Vision / multimodal cannot give a text-only model new abilities.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The secondary preset points to a real image-capable model.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Choose your
vision helper
scenes.body: Open Settings → Voice & Vision → Screen & desktop control. Under Secondary vision model, select that saved preset. It has its own provider, connection and model.
scenes.callout: Secondary vision model: choose a tested preset
scenes.note: Step 3 of 7 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Choose your
vision helper
scenes.body: A cloud helper can receive pictures even when your main language model runs locally; choose a local helper if you want that image processing local.
scenes.callout: Secondary vision model: choose a tested preset
scenes.note: Step 3 of 7 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A local
helper example
items: Primary: your working text-only local model
Secondary: your tested local image model
Choose its preset under Secondary vision model
Save the intended Voice & Vision settings
scenes.note: A cloud helper receives images even with a local primary. Choose a local helper if you want these model calls local.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The intended image model is selected.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Choose the
image route
scenes.body: Auto: primary → secondary fallback uses the resolved model if it can accept images, and the secondary when needed.
scenes.callout: Vision routing: Auto, secondary, disabled or legacy
scenes.note: Step 4 of 7 · Teaching 1 of 3. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Choose the
image route
scenes.body: Always use secondary preset sends every image through the selected helper. Disabled turns image-model routing off.
scenes.callout: Vision routing: Auto, secondary, disabled or legacy
scenes.note: Step 4 of 7 · Teaching 2 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Choose the
image route
scenes.body: The Legacy options exist for older dedicated configurations; a saved secondary preset is easier to manage.
scenes.callout: Vision routing: Auto, secondary, disabled or legacy
scenes.note: Step 4 of 7 · Teaching 3 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Understand
the route choices
items: Auto: resolved primary, then secondary if needed
Always secondary: every image uses the helper
Disabled: no image-model routing
Legacy: older dedicated configurations
scenes.note: The resolved primary can be the effective backup model. Review the actual route instead of assuming a saved name determines it.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The selected routing choice matches what you want.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Check the route.
Try a picture.
scenes.body: Click Save changes and check Effective route. A model may say it will be tested on first use until image input has been verified.
scenes.callout: Effective route: first-use verification status
scenes.note: Step 5 of 7 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Check the route.
Try a picture.
scenes.body: Attach a simple picture and ask “Describe what you see.” Confirm the description is right before asking it to reason about a tiny label or complicated screen.
scenes.callout: Effective route: first-use verification status
scenes.note: Step 5 of 7 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Test a
simple picture
items: Save changes and read Effective route
First-use status may still be unverified
Attach a simple picture and Send your question
Ask: “Describe what you see.”
scenes.note: Confirm the description against the picture. A status declaration is not a successful first image response.
